title: 14th India-Nepal Joint Working Group Meeting Held in Dehradun
body_text:
The 14 th meeting of the India-Nepal Joint Working Group (JWG) was held on 20–21 August 2026 in Dehradun.
The Indian delegation was led by Ms. Pausumi Basu, Joint Secretary (BM-I), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India. The Nepali delegation was led by Mr. Ananda Kafle, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of Nepal.
Both sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral cooperation on border management and security, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in these areas.
Discussions covered addressing trans-border crime and criminal activities; the strengthening and effective utilisation of border infrastructure, particularly Integrated Check Posts (ICPs), roads and railway networks; and the removal of encroachments and maintenance of boundary pillars.
The two sides also exchanged views on strengthening institutional coordination and capacity building across various sectors, and agreed to sustain engagement in these areas.
It was agreed that the next meeting of the Joint Working Group will be held in Nepal at a mutually convenient date.

enrichment.summary: The 14th India-Nepal Joint Working Group (JWG) meeting was held in Dehradun on 20–21 August 2026, led by Joint Secretary Pausumi Basu (India) and Joint Secretary Ananda Kafle (Nepal). Both sides reviewed bilateral cooperation on border management and security, discussing trans-border crime, border infrastructure like Integrated Check Posts, encroachment removal, and boundary pillar maintenance. They agreed to sustain institutional coordination and capacity building, with the next meeting to be held in Nepal.
enrichment.context: The India-Nepal border, spanning over 1,800 km, is open and largely unfenced, facilitating free movement of people under the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship but also posing challenges related to smuggling, human trafficking, counterfeit currency circulation, and other trans-border crimes. The JWG on Border Management is a periodic institutional mechanism between the two countries' Home Ministries to address these issues, alongside boundary pillar disputes (a recurring irritant, especially around areas like Kalapani, Susta, and Lipulekh) and infrastructure development such as Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) at points like Raxaul-Birgunj and Jogbani-Biratnagar. This routine, procedural meeting reaffirms ongoing cooperation without announcing new agreements, treaties, or policy shifts, making it primarily an administrative update on an established bilateral mechanism.
